evidence.note: Repeatedly abandons the 'comprehensive big-bang' approach (deletes main.rs at 20, 23, 33 on unresolved-field breakage) and pivots to an incrementally-grown foundation — decisive course-change when an approach is falsified, though at the build-method level.
Root-cause diagnosis of inverted multidim array type representation (Arr(Arr(int,2),1)) and fix of the type-construction order — a structural fix to the type model, not a symptom patch.

Targeted redesigns of affected areas: adds function-return-type tracking + arg/return type-conversion machinery; replaces global struct namespace with scope-tracked tags (new SE::Tag) to fix a structural collision. Anchor-5/8 behavior.
Attempts struct-return ABI, detects it as a structural feature, sees a regression (96.8→96.4), and reverts decisively rather than patching the broken change — avoiding stubborn patching.

Clusters remaining failures by feature (bitfields, vectors, complex, struct return) and explicitly distinguishes local bugs from structural limitations, reasoning about which are worth the redesign cost — but ultimately declines the biggest structural redesigns.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 3: beyond local fixes it performs several genuine targeted redesigns of affected areas (type representation, type-conversion infrastructure, scoped struct tags) and reverts a regression-causing change rather than patching around it, plus it clusters failures by root cause and separates local bugs from structural limitations (anchor-8 traits). It falls short of a clean 8/10 because the largest structural limitations (struct-return ABI, bitfields, vectors) are correctly diagnosed but left unimplemented, and much of the mid-game is local symptom-patching. This places observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at 6.
